work.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
work.creator: J. K. Rowling

summary: A school story of belonging, friendship, and wonder, in which an unloved boy finds a home, faces fear and a hidden enemy, and longs for lost parents.

need-to-breathe.why: Devil's Snare wraps round Harry and Ron until Hermione conjures fire, and Quirrell's hands close on Harry's throat before they blister.

hungry.why: The Dursleys send Harry to his cupboard without meals, Hagrid brings him a squashed birthday cake, and the Hogwarts feasts astonish a boy who never had enough.

full.why: After the welcome feast Harry is too full to move, and Dudley's fat and tantrums are the Dursleys' idea of plenty.

need-to-poop.why: The troll is cornered in a girls' bathroom, but no one needs it.

sleepy.why: Fluffy sleeps to the sound of Hagrid's flute, Harry dreams of a turban that talks and a flash of green light, and the dormitory nights frame the year.

nauseous.why: No one is sickened; Ron's slug-vomiting belongs to a later book.

dizzy.why: Harry's broom bucks and rolls under Quirrell's jinx during his first match, and Neville falls from his broom in the first flying lesson.

fatigued.why: Harry is drained after facing Quirrell and sleeps three days in the hospital wing; exertion otherwise is Quidditch practice.

pain.why: Harry's scar sears whenever Quirrell's turban is near, Quirrell's hands blister at Harry's touch, and Neville breaks his wrist falling off his broom.

disgusted.why: The troll reeks of old socks and public toilets and leaves troll bogies on Harry's wand, Snape's hair is greasy, and Voldemort's face on the back of Quirrell's head horrifies Harry.

too-hot-too-cold.why: The Dursleys' flight ends in a freezing shack on a rock in a storm, and the Hogwarts winter freezes the lake, but cold is scenery.

afraid.why: Harry faces a three-headed dog, a mountain troll, a hooded figure drinking unicorn blood in the forest, and Voldemort's face on Quirrell's head.

anxious.why: Harry fears being sorted into Slytherin, dreads Snape's lessons and the exams, and lies awake worrying that Snape will steal the Stone.

panic.why: Hermione panics in the Devil's Snare until Ron shouts that she is a witch, and the school stampedes when Quirrell announces the troll in the dungeons.

sensory-pleasures.why: Harry gorges on his first Hogwarts feast, buys the whole sweets trolley, and finds flying the one thing he can do without being taught.

aesthetic-pleasures.why: Harry gazes at the Great Hall's ceiling bewitched to look like the sky, and at Diagon Alley's shop windows.

piquancy.why: One Every Flavor Bean tastes of pepper; spice goes no further.

fun-excitement.why: Quidditch, the flying lesson where Harry catches Neville's Remembrall, wizard chess with Ron, and Fred and George's snowballs make the year a joy.

love-romantic.why: Eleven-year-olds have no romance; Harry's parents' love is remembered, not shown.

love-family.why: Harry sees his dead parents in the Mirror of Erised, Mrs Weasley knits him a sweater, and his mother's dying love is the magic that burns Quirrell.

grief.why: Harry sits night after night before the Mirror of Erised looking at the parents he lost, and Hagrid gives him a photograph album of them at the end.

missing-someone.why: The Mirror shows Harry the family he has missed all his life, and Dumbledore must warn him not to waste away before it.

liking-as-a-friend.why: Ron shares his sandwiches and Harry his sweets on the train, the troll turns Hermione from a nightmare into a friend, and the three go through the trapdoor together.

empathy.why: Harry sees Neville's misery under Malfoy's bullying and Hagrid's grief at giving up Norbert, and Dumbledore reads Harry's longing at the Mirror.

compassion.why: Hagrid carries Harry out of the Dursleys' life, Harry and Ron go back for Hermione when the troll corners her, and the trio helps Hagrid send Norbert away.

grateful.why: Harry is overwhelmed by Mrs Weasley's Christmas sweater, and Hermione thanks the boys by lying to the teachers about the troll.

pleasure-from-helping.why: Hermione delights in helping with homework and the Flamel search, and Hagrid in doing things for Harry.

trustful-distrustful.why: Harry, Ron, and Hermione are sure Snape is the villain and trust stammering Quirrell, the Dursleys lie to Harry about his parents, and a hooded stranger tricks Hagrid into revealing how to pass Fluffy.

depressed.why: At the Dursleys Harry has no one, sleeps in a cupboard, and has had no birthday for ten years, a lack the Hogwarts letter ends.

angry.why: Uncle Vernon rages at the letters until he flees to a rock in the sea, Harry flies after Malfoy in fury, and Ron goes red at every insult to his family.

envious.why: Ron sees himself in the Mirror as Head Boy holding the Quidditch Cup, Malfoy seethes at Harry's Seeker post, and Dudley counts his presents.

jealous-friendship.why: Malfoy offers Harry his friendship and is refused for Ron, and Ron bristles at Hermione's intrusion before the troll.

hatred.why: Snape seems to hate Harry from the first potions lesson, Harry and Malfoy loathe each other, and the Dursleys hate everything to do with magic.

contempt.why: Malfoy sneers at the Weasleys' poverty and Hagrid's hut, Snape mocks Harry as our new celebrity, and the Dursleys treat Harry as a freak.

resentment.why: Harry burns at Snape docking points unfairly, Ron at Slytherin winning the cup seven years running, and the whole house at McGonagall's fifty-point penalty.

proud.why: Gryffindor wins the House Cup, Harry becomes the youngest Seeker in a century, Hermione lives for marks, and Malfoy boasts of his father.

amused.why: Hagrid gives Dudley a pig's tail, Fred and George bewitch snowballs to hit Quirrell's turban, and Peeves pelts the first years.

sense-of-belonging.why: Harry, the unwanted boy under the stairs, is sorted into Gryffindor, finds Hogwarts his first home, and dreads the summer return to Privet Drive.

lonely.why: Harry grew up with no friends because Dudley's gang chased them off, and Hermione cries in the bathroom because no one likes her.

judgy-moral-sense.why: Hermione agonizes over rule-breaking, Neville stands up to his friends and earns the winning ten points, and Dumbledore judges that what Harry did was right.

admiration.why: The wizarding world stares at the Boy Who Lived, Harry looks up to Dumbledore and Hagrid, and Hermione worships her teachers.

embarrassed.why: Harry blushes at the staring in the Leaky Cauldron and the Great Hall, Ron is ashamed of his secondhand robes, and Neville loses his toad and falls off his broom.

shame.why: Hagrid is ashamed to admit he was expelled, and Ron feels the shame of corned beef sandwiches and a hand-me-down wand.

guilt.why: Harry is a pariah after losing Gryffindor one hundred and fifty points, and Hagrid is stricken that he told a stranger how to get past Fluffy.

sad.why: Harry is sad before the Mirror and at the thought of returning to the Dursleys, and Hagrid sobs over Norbert.

happy.why: Harry's first year is the happiest of his life: friends, Quidditch, Christmas presents, and a place where he belongs.

joyful-euphoric.why: Harry nearly swallows the Snitch and wins, Gryffindor explodes at the House Cup, and Harry's first sight of Hogwarts across the lake is pure joy.

effort.why: The trio works through the obstacles under the trapdoor, Hermione drills them for exams, and Harry trains for Quidditch three nights a week.

focused-in-flow.why: Harry on a broom is wholly absorbed, Ron directs the giant chess game move by move, and Hermione works the potions riddle with cool focus.

bored.why: Professor Binns drones so that the class dozes, and the Dursleys' summer stretches before Harry as weeks of nothing.

distracted.why: Harry's mind wanders in class to the Stone and the trapdoor, and he cannot stop thinking of the Mirror.

impatient.why: Harry counts the days until September first and until his first match, and cannot wait to get back to the Mirror.

curious.why: Harry, Ron, and Hermione hunt the library for Nicolas Flamel, explore the forbidden corridor, and cannot leave the package from vault 713 alone.

surprised.why: Hagrid tells Harry he is a wizard, Harry finds Quirrell rather than Snape at the Mirror, and Dumbledore's last-minute points snatch the Cup from Slytherin.

awe.why: Harry walks through Diagon Alley wishing he had eight more eyes, sees Hogwarts lit across the lake, and watches the Great Hall's floating candles.

skeptical-doubtful.why: Hermione doubts the boys' theories until the evidence mounts, Hagrid insists Snape would never, and the Dursleys refuse to believe in magic at all.

feeling-of-knowing.why: Harry knows he has read the name Nicolas Flamel somewhere and cannot place it until he turns over the Chocolate Frog card.

confused.why: Harry is baffled by Hagrid's revelations, by Platform Nine and Three-Quarters, and by the Mirror's backward inscription.

frustrated.why: The letters keep coming and Vernon keeps burning them, the trio cannot find Flamel for months, and Harry cannot control his jinxed broom.

uncertain-certain.why: Harry decides to go through the trapdoor despite expulsion, and the trio is certain, wrongly, that Snape is the thief.

understanding.why: Harry understands why Quirrell cannot touch him when Dumbledore explains his mother's love, and why the Mirror gave the Stone only to one who would not use it.

inspired.why: Hermione thinks of fire for the Devil's Snare, Harry spots the key with the crumpled wing, and Ron sees that he must be taken for Harry to win.

satisfied.why: The Stone is destroyed, Voldemort is driven off, Gryffindor takes the House Cup, and Harry goes home with a photo album and a threat to use on Dudley.

foreboding.why: Harry's dreams of green light, the centaurs reading war in Mars, and Hagrid's fear of Voldemort's name all warn that worse is coming.

nostalgia.why: Hagrid's photo album and the Mirror give Harry a past he never had; little else looks back.

anticipation-suspense.why: The trio waits for Snape to make his move, Harry waits for the Hogwarts letter the Dursleys keep burning, and the trapdoor's obstacles unfold one by one.

hope.why: Harry hopes for the letter, for a family in the Mirror, and that Gryffindor can still win the Cup.

schadenfreude.why: Harry and Ron savor Malfoy's detention in the forest and Dudley's pig tail, and grin at Snape limping from Fluffy's bite.

elevation.why: Ron sacrifices himself on the chessboard, Neville stands up to his friends, and Harry's mother died to save him.

rage.why: Uncle Vernon goes purple and boards up the letterbox, and Harry dives after Malfoy for Neville's Remembrall in a flash of fury.
